meridianR

An R interface to Google Meridian, a Bayesian Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) library. meridianR wraps the Meridian Python package with reticulate, following the design of keras3: faithful bindings to Meridian’s data, model, and analysis objects, plus an idiomatic R layer with tidy data in and out, S3 print()/summary(), and pipe-friendly verbs.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Roeh-Marketing/meridianR")

Then provision the Python side (Meridian and its JAX / TensorFlow stack) once:

library(meridianR)
install_meridian()

install_meridian(gpu = TRUE) installs the CUDA build, and install_meridian(meridian_version = "1.7.1") pins an older supported release. If no suitable Python (3.11–3.13) is found, one is installed first (via uv when available). If you skip this step, reticulate provisions an environment automatically on first use.

Quick start 

library(meridianR)

# 1. Assemble input data from a long-format data frame
input <- as_meridian_input(
  sales,
  kpi            = "conversions",
  time           = "week",
  geo            = "region",
  population     = "population",
  media_spend    = c("tv_spend", "search_spend"),
  media_channels = c("TV", "Search"),
  controls       = "price_index"
)

# 2. Configure priors and the model specification. `conversions` is a
#    non-revenue KPI, so a scale-free contribution prior ("TV drives ~13% of
#    conversions, Search ~6%") is easier to reason about than an ROI prior.
spec <- model_spec(
  max_lag          = 8,
  knots            = 10,
  media_prior_type = "contribution",
  prior            = prior_distribution(contribution_m = prior_beta(c(3, 2), c(20, 30)))
)

# 3. Fit
mmm <- meridian_model(input, spec)
fit(mmm, n_chains = 4, n_adapt = 1000, n_burnin = 500, n_keep = 1000)

summary(mmm)
rhat_summary(mmm)
plot_roi(mmm)

See vignette("getting-started") and vignette("analysis") for the full walkthrough, and scripts/learn_meridianR.R in the source repository for a guided tour of every prior (including adstock) with prior-vs-posterior experiments.

Choosing the Python environment

Meridian needs Python 3.11–3.13, and install_meridian() provisions it together with tested Meridian releases in the range 1.7.1 through 2.2.1 in the r-meridian virtual environment. It installs 2.2.1 by default. The boundary versions have passed the integration suite; intermediate releases are included in the supported range but are not individually listed in the test matrix yet. You can choose an exact version in this range with meridian_version. When Meridian is first imported, meridianR warns if the active environment holds a release outside this window.

meridianR uses Meridian’s default backend: JAX from Meridian 2.2 (where TensorFlow is deprecated upstream), TensorFlow before that. use_backend("tensorflow") or use_backend("jax") overrides it; call it before Meridian is first imported.

save_model() writes Meridian’s versioned schema format for .binpb / .txtpb paths (readable across Meridian versions) and the legacy pickle format for .pkl paths.

reticulate can only bind one Python per R session, and an interpreter pinned by RETICULATE_PYTHON or your IDE takes precedence over meridianR’s default. If another Python is initialized first you will see:

ERROR: The requested version of Python (...) cannot be used, as another version
of Python (...) has already been initialized.

To fix it, point reticulate at r-meridian before anything else touches Python, then restart R:

  • In RStudio: Tools -> Global Options -> Python -> Select -> Virtual Environments -> r-meridian (or set it per project), then restart the session.

  • In a fresh session, as the first line:

    reticulate::use_virtualenv("r-meridian", required = TRUE)
library(meridianR)

meridianR warns at load time when RETICULATE_PYTHON points elsewhere.

Python warnings

Meridian emits warnings through Python’s warnings module, which normally print raw (file path, line number, and all). meridianR reroutes them so they appear as ordinary R warnings of class meridian_python_warning – cli-formatted and silenceable with suppressWarnings(). To keep the raw Python output instead, set options(meridianR.reformat_warnings = FALSE) before first use.

Status

meridianR is in early development. The current release covers data loading, model specification, priors, MCMC fitting, and analysis (tidy metrics and ggplot2 charts). Budget optimization is on the roadmap.

Everything in Meridian remains reachable through the meridian module handle, the low-level escape hatch beneath the wrappers.
